data.title: Choose the correct answer for each question.
data.description: Practise maintaining logical flow and choosing language appropriate to formal, neutral and informal contexts.
learningPoints: Keep pronoun and reference chains clear across sentences.
Use consistent levels of formality within a text.
Choose formal alternatives for academic and professional writing.
Avoid abrupt topic shifts and unsupported ideas.
Use cohesive links that reflect the intended relationship.
Match tone and register to audience and purpose.

sections.summary: Choosing formal wording in a report.
sections.explain: Formal reports prefer neutral, precise language.

words.word: The results indicate that further research is required.
The results kind of show we need to look into it more.
The results are, like, saying more research is needed.

sections.summary: Choosing informal wording in a message to a friend.
sections.explain: Informal personal messages can use contractions and conversational phrasing.

words.word: I can't make it tonight, but I'll call you tomorrow.
I regret to inform you that I am unable to attend this evening.
Attendance shall not be possible on my behalf tonight.

sections.explain: Reference words should clearly point back to the intended noun or idea.

words.word: The company introduced flexible hours. This improved staff morale.
The company introduced flexible hours. He improved staff morale.
The company introduced flexible hours. They improved it, with no clear referent.

sections.explain: A coherent paragraph should develop one central topic.

words.word: The scheme reduced traffic. It also lowered air pollution in the city centre.
The scheme reduced traffic. My cousin is learning Italian.
The scheme reduced traffic. However because yesterday.

sections.explain: Formal correspondence often uses polite, indirect phrasing.

words.word: I would be grateful if you could provide further details.
Send me more details when you get a chance.
Give me the info ASAP.

sections.explain: Avoid mixing highly formal and very casual language without a reason.

words.word: The proposal is unlikely to succeed unless additional funding is secured.
The proposal is unlikely to succeed unless we get loads more cash.
The proposal's gonna fail unless additional funding is secured herein.

sections.explain: Choose a linker that accurately connects contrasting ideas.

words.word: The course is demanding; however, it is extremely rewarding.
The course is demanding; therefore, it is extremely rewarding as a contrast.
The course is demanding; for example, it is rewarding.

sections.explain: Professional communication should be clear without being excessively casual or emotional.

words.word: There appears to be an error in the latest invoice.
You've totally messed up the latest invoice.
I am absolutely furious beyond belief about this invoice!

sections.explain: Each sentence should follow logically from the one before it.

words.word: Sales declined in the first quarter. As a result, the company reduced production.
Sales declined in the first quarter. In contrast, the company reduced production as a result.
Sales declined in the first quarter. My office has three windows.

sections.summary: Choosing register for an academic conclusion.
sections.explain: Academic conclusions should summarise cautiously and objectively.

words.word: Overall, the evidence suggests that the policy has been moderately effective.
Basically, the policy worked pretty well.
The policy was awesome and totally did the job.
